:::{#thm-surprisal-neg-log-prob}
#### Surprisal is the negative logarithm of the probability

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv),
and let $x$ be a [value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) of $X$ with $\P(X=x) > 0$.
Then the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $x$ is the negative of the [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) of its [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability):

$$\surprisalf{x} = -\logf{\P(X=x)}.$$ {#eq-thm-surprisal-neg-log-prob}

:::

::: proof

$$
\begin{aligned}
\surprisalf{x}
&= \logf{\rarityf{x}} && \text{(definition of surprisal)} \\
&= \logf{\frac{1}{\P(X=x)}} && \text{(definition of rarity)} \\
&= -\logf{\P(X=x)}. && \text{(logarithm of a reciprocal)}
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-thm-surprisal-neg-log-prob-2}

:::
